rationale: Evidence across molecularly confirmed GTPBP2 cases confirms that basal ganglia iron accumulation is not an early universal hallmark of Jaberi-Elahi syndrome, but rather a variable, age-dependent finding present in only a minority of reported individuals. The systematic literature review by Manoochehri et al. (2024) across 28 patients demonstrated that core manifestations are early-onset neurodevelopmental features (motor delay in 26/28, sparse hair in 26/28, speech disorder in 24/28, intellectual disability in 23/28, and hypotonia in 23/28), whereas radiologically documented brain iron accumulation was restricted to an older subset (4/28 patients, all aged 19-30 years) originally identified in the index Iranian kindred by Jaberi et al. (2016). Younger pediatric individuals consistently fail to display pallidal T2 hypointensity despite profound cerebellar and optic atrophy.

evidence.text: In a cohort review of 28 individuals with Jaberi-Elahi syndrome, brain iron accumulation was not a universal early feature, whereas early manifestations were dominated by motor development delay (26/28), sparse hair (26/28), speech disorder (24/28), intellectual disability (23/28), hypotonia (23/28), skeletal abnormalities (23/28), and visual impairment (18/28). Brain iron accumulation was documented only in an older subset of patients aged 19 to 30 years.

source.title: Jaberi-Elahi syndrome: Exploring a novel GTPBP2 mutation and a literature review
source.quote: A large numbers of patients manifest motor development delay (26/28), sparse hair (26/28), and speech disorder (24/28). Moreover, a significant fraction of patients suffer from intellectual disability (23/28), hypotonia (23/28), skeletal problems (23/28), and visual impairment (18/28).

evidence.text: The original description of GTPBP2 as a putative NBIA-associated gene was identified in an adult consanguineous Iranian family with 3 affected siblings exhibiting brain iron deposition in the basal ganglia together with intellectual disability and retinal dysfunction.

source.title: Identification of mutation in GTPBP2 in patients of a family with neurodegeneration accompanied by iron deposition in the brain
source.quote: We aimed to identify the genetic cause of a neurologic disorder accompanied with mental deficiency in a consanguineous family with 3 affected siblings by linkage analysis and exome sequencing. Iron accumulation in the brain of the patients was a notable phenotypic feature.

evidence.text: GTPBP2 is recognized as an NBIA-associated gene based on findings in an Iranian kindred, but broad NBIA cohorts demonstrate marked clinical and age-dependent heterogeneity.

source.title: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation and a brief report of the disease in Iran
source.quote: one of the latest discovered NBIA genes, GTP-binding protein 2 (GTPBP2), has been identified in an Iranian family, and there are some patients who have genetically remained unknown.

new_directions.question_text: At what specific age threshold does susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) or T2* MRI reliably detect basal ganglia iron accumulation in GTPBP2-deficient patients?
new_directions.rationale: Because pediatric patients present with severe cerebellar and retinal degeneration without basal ganglia iron deposition, prospective longitudinal SWI/QSM neuroimaging across ages 5-25 is required to establish the exact natural history of iron accumulation.

new_directions.question_text: What differentiates the cellular iron handling pathway in GTPBP2-related neurodegeneration from canonical NBIA forms like PKAN and PLAN?
new_directions.rationale: GTPBP2 functions in ribosomal stalling and translational surveillance rather than canonical iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis or lipid/coenzyme A metabolism, indicating that pallidal iron accumulation may be a secondary bystander effect of chronic neurodegeneration rather than primary iron dysregulation.
